m.chalisa.do1: O Śrī Bhairava, remover of troubles, bringer of good, merciful one: compassionate to the lowly, have mercy night and day on your servant.
m.chalisa.cau1: Victory to you, bearer of the ḍamaru, large-eyed one; your colour is dark and your body most fearsome.
m.chalisa.cau2: Victory to the bearer of the trident, victory to the bearer of the ḍamaru, the kotwāl (guardian) of Kāśī, remover of troubles.
m.chalisa.cau3: Victory to the son of Girijā, supremely merciful; remover of troubles, take away the net of delusion.
m.chalisa.cau4: Victory to Baṭuka Bhairava, remover of fear; victory to Kāla Bhairava, the mighty.
m.chalisa.cau5: All sing of your eight forms, each more fruitful than the last.
m.chalisa.cau6: You are Śiva's very form and Śiva's follower; you are lord of the gaṇas and the master of all.
m.chalisa.cau7: A crown graces your coil of matted hair; the moon on your forehead shines in great beauty.
m.chalisa.cau8: At your waist the girdle and its little bells ring; at the sight of you all fears flee.
m.chalisa.cau9: In your hands are a most beautiful trident and ḍamaru, and a charming whisk of peacock feathers.
m.chalisa.cau10: Mighty one, you hold a skull-bowl and a sword; your form, Lord, is described as four-armed.
m.chalisa.cau11: Your mount is a dog, and you are ever a store of happiness; Lord, you are endless, you are imperishable.
m.chalisa.cau12: Victory, victory, victory to Bhairava, breaker of fear; victory to the merciful one, delight of his devotees' hearts.
m.chalisa.cau13: Your eyes are large, red and very heavy; you are Śiva, the red-hued foe of Tripura.
m.chalisa.cau14: Crying bam bam bam day and night, you worship Śiva, the foe of the demons.
m.chalisa.cau15: In one form you were called Śiva; as the second, you took the form of Bhairava.
m.chalisa.cau16: You are the servant, and you are the Lord and Master; you are the indweller of the whole world.
m.chalisa.cau17: Your body is red; in some places you are known as dark.
m.chalisa.cau18: Again, you are described as white; you have three colours, O mine of virtues.
m.chalisa.cau19: The Lord's three eyes are supremely lovely; gods, men and sages all meditate on him.
m.chalisa.cau20: You wear the tiger's skin, Master of the world; you are lord of the ghosts, wholly free of desire.
m.chalisa.cau21: You are Cakranātha, fierce Nakuleśa, Nimiṣa and Digambara, and fierce is your fame.
m.chalisa.cau22: You are Krodhavatsa, lord of spirits and holder of Death; you are Cakratuṇḍa, ten-armed, the wearer of serpents.
m.chalisa.cau23: Lord, you have millions of names; repeated always, they wipe out heavy sorrows.
m.chalisa.cau24: The sixty-four yoginīs dance with you; you are wrathful, and you delight greatly in battle.
m.chalisa.cau25: You are Bhūtanātha, lord of spirits, and supremely holy; you are the future, you are the past.
m.chalisa.cau26: The present is your pure form; you are Time itself, supremely beyond compare.
m.chalisa.cau27: You removed Ailādī's trouble and accomplished the work of your devotee Sāda.
m.chalisa.cau28: Lord, you are called the son of Kālī; so I bow my head daily at your feet.
m.chalisa.cau29: Śrī Krodheśa, extend your grace; knowing me to be lowly, carry me across.
m.chalisa.cau30: Day and night I am drowning in the ocean of worldly existence; foe of the wicked, be merciful.
m.chalisa.cau31: Lord, knowing me to be your servant, be gracious; grant me now devotion to you.
m.chalisa.cau32: May I always serve Bhairava; what other god is like you?
m.chalisa.cau33: Aśvanātha, you are supremely charming; to the wicked, Lord, you are terrible.
m.chalisa.cau34: Wherever any servant of yours may be, no trouble befalls him.
m.chalisa.cau35: Lord, take away your devotee's pain; who, Lord, is a mighty hero like you?
m.chalisa.cau36: Forgive all my offences; knowing me to be lowly, make me your own.
m.chalisa.cau37: Whoever recites this Chālīsā, be gracious to him, O Lord of the world.
m.chalisa.do2: Victory to Bhairava, victory to the lord of spirits; victory, victory, victory to the root of happiness. Be ever gracious to your servant, and always grant him joy.
